incident: Nitrogen campaign drops Sliver and ends with BlackCat/ALPHV ransomware (DFIR Report, intrusion Nov 2023, published 2024-09-30)

sources.title: Nitrogen Campaign Drops Sliver and Ends With BlackCat Ransomware - The DFIR Report (2024-09-30)
sources.what_it_gave: entry point (malvertised fake Advanced IP Scanner -> Nitrogen/Sliver on beachhead), hops (Impacket wmiexec to servers, DCs via xcopy/WMIC/PsExec), exfil (Restic to 195.123.226.84 Bulgaria), TTR ~156h / 8 days, BlackCat domain-wide via PsExec+safeboot

narrative_before: In November 2023 a user searching for Advanced IP Scanner downloaded a trojanized installer from a Google-ad-promoted fake site; the Nitrogen loader side-loaded a malicious Python DLL and dropped a Sliver beacon on the beachhead (DFIR Report). Within minutes the actor ran net/ipconfig/nltest discovery, then added Cobalt Strike beacons, SharpHound and PowerSploit enumeration, and dumped LSASS to obtain local-admin then domain-admin credentials. Using Impacket wmiexec they moved to a first server, downloaded a tool ZIP via curl, re-established scheduled-task/registry persistence, then repeated on a second server, a file server and a backup server. About six hours in, Restic was deployed on the file server and exfiltrated share data to a REST server at 195.123.226.84 in Bulgaria. After a quiet period, on day seven they reviewed the backup console; on day eight they xcopied tools to a domain controller, ran a batch script via PsExec to reset a privileged backup service-account password, pushed the BlackCat binary via SMB/copy, and ran a second script via PsExec on hosts from pc.txt that set safeboot-with-networking, a RunOnce key and Winlogon autologon before rebooting into Safe Mode to encrypt. Time to ransomware was about 156 hours over 8 days (DFIR Report).

detection_moments.description: Initial compromise: trojanized Advanced IP Scanner side-loads Nitrogen, drops Sliver beacon on the beachhead; hands-on discovery begins ~8 minutes later.
detection_moments.evidence: 'the attacker initiated hands-on keyboard discovery... Two minutes later, additional Sliver beacons were deployed on the compromised host' - Nitrogen Campaign, DFIR Report

detection_moments.description: By ~6 hours in the actor had dumped domain-admin creds, moved via wmiexec to two servers, the file server and backup server, and started Restic exfiltration before activity went quiet until day 7.
detection_moments.evidence: 'The threat actor continued their lateral movement, replicating the same actions on both a file server and a backup server. Approximately six hours after gaining initial access, they deployed the open-source backup tool Restic on the file server.' - Nitrogen Campaign, DFIR Report

attack_path: Impacket wmiexec with LSASS-dumped local-admin creds; curl tool download, scheduled-task/registry persistence - T1047 / T1003.001 / T1021.002
lateral movement to file server; Restic exfiltration to REST server 195.123.226.84 (Bulgaria) over HTTP - T1021.002 / T1567 / T1048
xcopy tools to DC, remote exec via WMIC, up.bat via PsExec resets privileged backup service account - T1021.002 / T1047 / T1569.002 / T1098
BlackCat binary copied over SMB/C$, 1.bat via PsExec sets safeboot+RunOnce+Winlogon autologon, reboot into Safe Mode to encrypt - T1021.002 / T1569.002 / T1486 / T1490
ambiguities: Report does not state victim detection; m1 = initial Nitrogen/Sliver execution, m2 = end of first active phase (exfil start) before the day-7 lull.
Number of hosts in pc.txt receiving BlackCat ('across the network', 'multiple remote hosts') not quantified; represented as pc_1..pc_3 (3 generic).
Number of domain controllers: 'the domain controllers' identified but tools pushed to 'one of the domain controllers'; modelled as one.

workstation->dc / workstation->files links not added for pc_1..pc_3 because the report does not describe those hosts using domain credentials toward DC/file server; they only receive the payload from the DC/staging server.
